episodes.167776: A lightning strike caused a fire at an apartment complex.
episodes.167777: A cold front pushed into an unseasonably warm and humid airmass over central Pennsylvania during the afternoon of May 22, 2022, generating showers and thunderstorms. The initial line of showers and storms formed well ahead of the front, and produced all of the severe weather. A second round of showers with the actual frontal passage (and isolated thunder across the Lower Susquehanna Valley) was much more benign.
episodes.167778: There were numerous late night through early morning marine thunderstorm wind gusts.
episodes.167827: A man walking along along Wilson Parrish Road in Umatilla in Lake County was slightly injured when lightning struck a nearby pole. The disoriented man was taken to a local hospital and was released later that day.
episodes.167867: Scattered to numerous shower and thunderstorms developed along a boundary moving north into southern middle Tennessee during the afternoon into the early evening hours. One storm became severe and took on a supercell type structure producing significant wind damage in eastern Lawrence county and possibly northwest Morgan county. This storm also produced quarter size hail in Lawrence county.
episodes.167885: A line of convection lifted north into the CSRA during the late afternoon and early evening hours on May 22nd in a moderately unstable environment with a weak shortwave lifting northward into the area. A few damaging wind reports occurred in Aiken County.
episodes.167965: Afternoon thunderstorms produce heavy rainfall leading to localized street flooding in Hernando County.
episodes.167980: A pre-frontal trough caused isolated thunderstorms to form in eastern Massachusetts during the late afternoon. But a scattered line of severe thunderstorms impacted western and central Massachusetts during the evening, in association with an approaching cold front.
episodes.168028: One lone supercell thunderstorm moved from north to south across Zapata and western Starr County early in the afternoon of May 22nd. This storm produced prolific rain rates and caused some street flooding and also produced sub-severe hail up to the size of a penny.
episodes.168051: A cold front approached the eastern mid-Atlantic late on May 22. Ahead of the front, a warm and strongly unstable air mass was present. However, wind shear was fairly weak and frontal forcing was not overly strong. As the front moved east, a couple areas of thunderstorms developed with daytime heating, gradually progressing eastward from late afternoon through the evening. As supported by the environment, some storms became strong to marginally severe with a few instances of damaging wind. Storm activity gradually waned by the later evening hours with loss of heating, and the frontal passage brought quieter weather by the following day.
episodes.168052: A cold front swept through Central New York, triggering thunderstorms along the boundary. The environment was favorable for severe weather and a couple isolated storms did have strong wind gusts. Most of the damage included large trees knocked over onto roadways.
episodes.168054: A cold front swept through Northeastern Pennsylvania, triggering thunderstorms along the boundary. One isolated cell produced strong gusts, knocking over a tree in Bradford County.

episodes.168246: A strong cold front produced multiple rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms resulting in isolated large hail and scattered wind damage.
episodes.168250: A gust front produced gale-force wind gusts over portions of the tidal Potomac River and middle Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.168252: Multiple lines of thunderstorms produced gale- to storm-force winds over much of the tidal Potomac River and portions of the Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.168763: On the morning of the 21st, a cold front extended southwestward from southern ON to far-northwestern OH. This front drifted southeastward through the early evening, when it became located in vicinity of the major axis of Lake Erie, west-central OH, and east-central IN. The front then moved little through the wee hours of the 22nd. A line of thunderstorms moved generally eastward across northwest PA during the early evening and generated isolated straight-line wind damage. The ambient environment consisted of moderate to strong effective bulk shear, MUCAPE, and DCAPE, respectively. Repeated thunderstorms training over the same areas of Erie and Crawford Counties in PA led to excessive rainfall and flash flooding. Total rainfall amounts of 3 to 5 inches were estimated by radar in these locations.
episodes.168803: An upper-level trough and slow-moving cold front pushed through the Mid-South on May 21, 2022. A warm and moist air mass was in place ahead of the front. Showers and thunderstorms developed in the afternoon into the evening. Large hail, damaging wind, and heavy rain were the result.
episodes.168805: An upper-level trough and slow-moving cold front pushed through the Mid-South on May 21, 2022. A warm and moist air mass was in place ahead of the front. Showers and thunderstorms developed in the afternoon into the evening. Large hail, damaging wind and heavy rain were the result.
episodes.168806: An upper-level trough and slow-moving cold front moved through the Mid-South on May 21, 2022. A warm and moist air mass was in place ahead of the front. Showers and thunderstorms developed in the afternoon into the evening. Large hail, damaging wind and heavy rain were the result.
episodes.168856: During the morning and afternoon hours of May 21st, the advection of warmth and moisture into the Upper Ohio Valley helped to build daytime instability.  A couple of thunderstorm lines developed ahead of an evening cold front. In an environment of sufficient shear, many reports of wind damage were received.
episodes.168903: A strong cold front approaching from the Ohio River Valley combined a warm and moist airmass produced clusters of thunderstorms across the region. One of these storms produced localized wind damage in Greenbrier County.
episodes.168905: A strong cold front approaching from the Ohio Valley combined with a moist and unstable airmass, triggered clusters of thunderstorms. A few of these storms produced damaging winds and localized hail.
episodes.168998: A weak upper level trough moved into much of Arkansas, Northeast and Central Texas, and North Louisiana during the afternoon and evening hours of May 21st, which helped to reinforce a weak cold front southeast into the region during the evening and overnight hours. The air mass ahead of the front was very unstable, with steep lapse rates present along the trough once large scale forcing was adequate enough to initiate shower and thunderstorm development. As a result, showers and thunderstorms quickly developed during the early to mid evening hours along and just ahead of the front, with many of these storms becoming severe across East Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and Northwest Louisiana. Damaging winds and isolated instances of large hail accompanied these storms, before they weakened by midnight that night as they moved into portions of North Louisiana.
episodes.168999: A weak upper level trough moved into much of Arkansas, Northeast and Central Texas, and North Louisiana during the afternoon and evening hours of May 21st, which helped to reinforce a weak cold front southeast into the region during the evening and overnight hours. The air mass ahead of the front was very unstable, with steep lapse rates present along the trough once large scale forcing was adequate enough to initiate shower and thunderstorm development. As a result, showers and thunderstorms quickly developed during the early to mid evening hours along and just ahead of the front, with many of these storms becoming severe across East Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and Northwest Louisiana. Damaging winds and isolated instances of large hail accompanied these storms as they moved across East Texas during the mid and late evening.  A second complex of severe thunderstorms developed over Central Texas near Waco, which quickly moved east into East Texas south of I-20. Damaging winds were widespread with the convective complex moving across Central and East Texas, before the winds weakened prior to reaching Western Louisiana by midnight on the 22nd.
episodes.169000: A weak upper level trough moved into much of Arkansas, Northeast and Central Texas, and North Louisiana during the afternoon and evening hours of May 21st, which helped to reinforce a weak cold front southeast into the region during the evening and overnight hours. The air mass ahead of the front was very unstable, with steep lapse rates present along the trough once large scale forcing was adequate enough to initiate shower and thunderstorm development. As a result, showers and thunderstorms quickly developed during the early to mid evening hours along and just ahead of the front, with many of these storms becoming severe across East Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and extreme Northwest Louisiana. Damaging winds and isolated instances of large hail accompanied these storms, with an isolated tornado briefly touching down just northwest of Hosston in Northern Caddo Parish. A second complex of severe thunderstorms developed over Central Texas near Waco, which quickly moved east into East Texas south of I-20. Damaging winds were widespread with the convective complex across Central and East texas, before the winds weakened as they reached extreme Northwest Louisiana around midnight. However, one isolated tornado did briefly touch down in Northern Caddo Parish near Hosston, before weakening during the early morning hours of the 22nd.
episodes.169022: Clusters of strong thunderstorms developed across portions of southeast Georgia in the afternoon ahead of an approaching cold front. These thunderstorms became strong enough to produce damaging wind gusts as the moved to the east.
episodes.169208: Minor flooding of the White River inundated some low-lying fields, including cropland. Several rounds of rain and thunderstorms on May 19th and again on May 21st brought heavy rainfall to southern Indiana. Lower portions of the White River rose above flood stage for a few days.
episodes.169364: A weak cold front moved into a moist and unstable airmass, resulting in scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms, a few of which were severe.
episodes.169369: A weak cold front moved into a moist and unstable airmass, resulting in scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms, a few of which were severe.
episodes.169374: A cold front brought a round of strong thunderstorms to the area with a few gusts measured in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.169436: A cold front was to our west and stalled out. A highly unstable air mass in place. Two rounds of severe weather occurred. The first was over the North Country and St. Lawrence Valley and aided by a well-developed vortex that had traversed the Toronto area early in the afternoon. The lake breeze off of Lake Erie protected the Buffalo metro area, but it ultimately interacted with the lake breeze and instability to the east of Lake Ontario. These storms produced mostly large hail. A second round of severe storms occurred later in the evening as a couple of passing waves triggered thunderstorms due to very high instability. Wind damage and heavy rain with some flooding were the main issues.  Most of this was from the Genesee Valley to the west as thunderstorms weakened once they pushed eastward after midnight.
episodes.169510: A cold front was to our west and stalled out. A highly unstable air mass in place. Two rounds of severe weather occurred. The first was over the North Country and St. Lawrence Valley and aided by a well-developed vortex that had traversed the Toronto area early in the afternoon. The lake breeze off of Lake Erie protected the Buffalo metro area, but it ultimately interacted with the lake breeze and instability to the east of Lake Ontario. These storms produced mostly large hail. A second round of severe storms occurred later in the evening as a couple of passing waves triggered thunderstorms due to very high instability. Wind damage and heavy rain with some flooding were the main issues. Most of this was from the Genesee Valley to the west as thunderstorms weakened once they pushed eastward after midnight.
episodes.169693: A broad upper level trough brought a cold front to South Central Texas and into a warm, moist airmass. Thunderstorms developed along the front and some of these storms produced large hail.
episodes.169798: A line of showers and thunderstorms resulted in numerous damaging wind reports over eastern New York during the evening hours on May 22.
episodes.169803: A line of showers and thunderstorms resulted in multiple damaging wind reports over northwestern Connecticut during the evening hours on May 22.
episodes.169804: A line of showers and thunderstorms resulted in multiple damaging wind reports over western Massachusetts during the evening hours on May 22.
episodes.169848: A surface trough over the North Carolina mountains, as well as a mid-level disturbance moving northeast out of Georgia and South Carolina, led to development of isolated to scattered showers and storms by the late afternoon and evening. Storms over the western Piedmont moved east-southeast, while storms tied to the disturbance tracked east-northeast into the Sandhills and Coastal Plain. All the storm activity was ahead of a southward moving cold front. One storm reached severe limits, produced a downed tree in Johnston County. Most storms died out after midnight.
episodes.169962: Severe thunderstorms formed along a pre-frontal trough just ahead of the a cold front in PA and NY. The storms headed east and moved through northeastern NJ bringing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.169969: A cold front crossed the region through the afternoon and evening of the 22nd. Thunderstorms developed in advance of the front. Isolated severe thunderstorms occurred across Downeast areas producing large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.169977: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed over western North Carolina during the afternoon and evening. A few of the storms produced large hail and brief damaging wind gusts.
episodes.169981: Scattered thunderstorms developed over the North Carolina mountains and foothills during the afternoon. One of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts in McDowell  County.
episodes.169996: A few thunderstorms developed early in the evening, with one particular storm becoming severe with some hail and damaging winds.
episodes.170027: Thunderstorms formed along a frontal boundary over south-central and southeast Texas on the afternoon and evening of the 21st. This activity moved toward the coast and reached the Victoria Crossroads during the early morning hours of the 22nd. The storms produced wind damage in Victoria and in Kingsville around daybreak on the 22nd.
episodes.170068: Strong thunderstorms over the southern Coastal Bend early in the morning on the 22nd became a bowing line of storms as it moved east across the bays south of Port Aransas and later across the Gulf waters. The storms produced wind gusts from 35 to 45 knots.
episodes.170095: The air mass on Saturday, May 21st, was becoming increasingly unstable in advance of a approaching cold front.  Modified morning soundings indicated a very unstable air mass by the afternoon. Surface based CAPE was in the 4000-4500 J/kg with enough dry air aloft for damaging downburst winds.  The severe threat would emerge again on Sunday as the cold front moved through Alabama.
episodes.170112: Scattered strong to severe storms formed into a line across portions of northwestern and northern Arkansas along and ahead of an advancing cold front. The line made it into central sections of the state by early evening, and into the south during the overnight hours of the 21st.||Dry weather and above normal temperatures returned to the state for a few days before yet another storm system would impact the state on the 21st. Ahead of a strong cold front, there was a risk of severe weather stretching from the Texas/Mexico border northeastward to the Maine/Canada border. Thunderstorms initially developed across north/northwest Arkansas before forming into a line and marching east. While a brief, weak tornado occurred across Newton County, the most widespread damage occurred across portions of north central into northeast Arkansas. Numerous trees were blown down from Sharp County into portions of Lawrence and Randolph Counties. Additional storms developed later during the evening of May 21st across portions of western into central and southern Arkansas. Severe weather reports weren't widespread, but a second brief tornado developed near Royal in Garland County.
episodes.170143: Scattered severe thunderstorms well in advance of a frontal boundary produced damaging winds across portions of south central and eastern Virginia.
episodes.170145: Scattered thunderstorms well in advance of a frontal boundary produced gusty winds across portions of the Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.170146: Scattered thunderstorms well in advance of a frontal boundary produced gusty winds across portions of the James River.
episodes.170147: Scattered thunderstorms well in advance of a frontal boundary produced gusty winds across portions of the York River.
episodes.170152: Isolated severe thunderstorm in advance of a frontal boundary produced damaging winds across portions of central Virginia.
episodes.170284: On May 21st, thunderstorms developed along a combination of a dryline and cold front across the southwestern portions of the region. These storms merged into an eastward moving complex of storms that produced strong winds across some of our Central Texas counties. On May 24th, numerous showers and storms affected the area due primarily to a series of boundaries and shortwaves. A complex of storms moved across parts of Central Texas but was weakening, and only one report of severe criteria winds was reported.
episodes.170448: An unseasonably hot and humid airmass was firmly in place across New England with highs well into the 80s across the interior mountains.  A pre-frontal trough ahead of an approaching cold front triggered a long line of severe thunderstorms that had a history of causing wind damage across Quebec province.  This line of storms reached the Maine border during the evening on May 21st.
episodes.170450: An unseasonably hot and humid airmass was firmly in place across New England with highs well into the 80s across the interior mountains. A pre-frontal trough ahead of an approaching cold front triggered a long line of severe thunderstorms that had a history of causing wind damage across Quebec province. This line of storms reached the New Hampshire border during the evening on May 21st.
episodes.170453: An unseasonably hot and humid airmass was firmly in place across New England with highs well into the 80s across the interior areas away from the coast. A surface cold front swung through the state during the afternoon triggering thunderstorms across interior areas.  A few of these storms became severe with damaging wind gusts and large hail being reported.
episodes.170457: An unseasonably hot and humid airmass was firmly in place across New England with highs well into the 80s across the interior areas away from the coast. episodes.170496: Scattered showers and thunderstorms affected parts of Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening hours on May 21, producing a few reports of large hail and wind damage.
episodes.170532: Warm moist air moved across the region with persistent, south to southwesterly surface flow, combined with moderate instability and shear, to produce several rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms across central Georgia.
episodes.171028: An ice jam which formed on the Yukon River 7 miles upstream of Grayling on May 15th resulted in Yukon River floodwaters draining into the Innoko River basin. The influx of water caused the Innoko River to rise overbank and cause minor flooding in the community of Shageluk.

Water levels on the Innoko River began rising to bankfull on Friday May 20th as floodwaters from an ice jam on the Yukon River started flowing into the Innoko River upstream of Shageluk. Water levels rose overbank in Shageluk on Saturday the 21st as the surge of water moved down the Innoko River, eventually cresting on Tuesday May 24th. Water levels in Shageluk remained above flood stage through May 30th with bankfull conditions persisting into the first week of June. Residents reported water over some roads near the river, including the road to the airport which was impassable and caused the airport to only be accessible by boat. The high water also caused significant erosion of some riverbanks.

In the Florence section of Northampton, a 50 foot by 50 foot wooden permanent pavilion structure was blown crooked at a landmark restaurant/tavern. The footings, which were lifted and bent, were attached by a metal bracket to concrete.  The pavilion can accomodate 18 tables with 4 people per table.  The building inspector classified the damage as $20,000.  Slightly farther to the southeast, a 50 ft by 75 ft. section of roofing, including insulation and rubber membrane, was peeled off of the Smith Vocational and Agricultural High School.  There was little in the way of water damage inside the school.  The Northampton building inspector rated the roof damage as $30,000.  Still farther to the southeast, a tree was down on Washington Avenue, as reported by amateur radio.
